newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices drop after gas build.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices drop after gas build.

text.p: U.S. energy futures prices fell moderately in after-hours trade Tuesday, following new inventory data that a showed a massive 3.6-million-barrel rise in gasoline stocks last week.
On NYMEX ACCESS, May gasoline futures slipped 0.70 cents a gallon overnight to 61.20 cents as 222 lots traded in May and 371 lots in all months by 2000 PDT, traders said.
"The market did not expect gasoline stocks to rise this much," a trader said. Analysts surveyed earlier by Reuters forecast a one million-barrel drop in gasoline.

After-hours volume was heavy, as 1,259 lots traded in May crude oil futures and 169 lots changed hands in May heating oil. Oil companies and locals took positions in the overnight market, traders said.

Crude oil for May delivery traded $19.56 a barrel several hours into ACCESS, down 27 cents a barrel from the market close, with traders pegging support at $18.96 a barrel tomorrow, and resistance at $19.30.
Some traders thought the market overeacted and would pare losses early Wednesday. "We've had some buying come in," one trader said, noting Wall Street speculators made the bids.
After-hours, NYMEX May heating oil traded at 54.10 cents, a 0.75-cent fall from the final daytime trade.
